title: Things to Do in Brijuni, Croatia: Top Attractions 2027
metaDescription: Top things to do in Brijuni National Park: Safari Park, Verige Roman villa, Tito exhibition, dinosaur footprints, cycling and tickets in euros.
content:
## What Are the Top Attractions in Brijuni?

Brijuni is a national park made up of 14 islands off the Istrian coast. Only Veliki Brijun is open for regular visits, and the park's own boat from Fažana is the standard way in. The crossing takes about 15 minutes. The main sights are the Safari Park, the Roman villa in Verige Bay, the Tito exhibitions, early Christian and Byzantine ruins, dinosaur footprints and a very old olive tree.

## Tickets and Getting There

The park ticket covers the return boat from Fažana, insurance, a guide, the tourist train, the Safari Park and the museum displays. The standard visit runs in a fixed slot of roughly four hours.

### Ticket prices for 2026–2027 (check the park website for any change)

- Guided excursion, adult: €50 from June to September, €35 from October to May.
- Students and over-65s: €40 in summer, €30 off-season.
- Children 7–18: €20 in summer, €15 off-season. Under-7s go free.
- Self-guided ticket with the Brijuni Pocket Guide app, adult: €40 in summer, €30 off-season.
- Evening entry from 6 pm in high season: €15.

Tickets are sold at the Fažana marina or on the park's official website. In July and August, buy online ahead of time because the busiest departures fill up. Fažana is about 8 km from Pula, and parking in the village gets scarce in August.

## Veliki Brijun Guided Tour by Tourist Train

The guided tour is the core of any visit. A small electric train and guide take visitors around the island for about an hour, with stops at the main sights. Tours run in Croatian, Italian, German and English. The same ticket also covers the exhibitions.

The tour feels scripted, especially in August, when groups move together. The self-guided ticket suits people who want to set their own pace. Both versions use the same boat and the same island.

## Safari Park

The Safari Park is the best-known attraction on Veliki Brijun. It began as Tito's private collection of animals, many of them gifts from foreign leaders. Today it holds zebras, Somali sheep, zebu cattle, dromedary camels, llamas and an elephant. The train passes through the park with a short stop, around ten minutes on a standard tour. Dogs are not allowed in the Safari Park, on the train or in the museums.

Fallow deer and mouflon also graze freely across the island's meadows, so wildlife is visible even outside the enclosure.

## Roman Villa in Verige Bay

The villa in Verige Bay dates from the 1st century AD. It is considered one of the finest Roman villas on the eastern Adriatic coast. The ruins sit directly on the water, and the cove is the most scenic stop on the circuit. Most of the walls are low, so the setting matters more than the structures. A mosaic from the villa is preserved in the Church of St. German.

## Tito on Brijuni Exhibition and the Museums

Tito used Veliki Brijun as a summer residence from 1947 until 1979. The photo exhibition *Josip Broz Tito on Brijuni* covers those years, including visits by world leaders. It is in a former steam bath building dating from the early 20th century. The same building holds an exhibition on Paul Kupelwieser, the last private owner, who developed the islands as a resort, and a natural history collection.

The Brijuni exhibitions present Tito in a very favorable light. Visitors wanting a more critical view of the period should read about it separately.

## Church of St. German and Other Historic Sites

The small Gothic Church of St. German dates from the 15th century. It holds copies of Istrian frescoes and Glagolitic inscriptions. The Basilica of St. Mary is the oldest Christian building on the island. The Byzantine Castrum is a fortified settlement with remains of a church. The Venetian castle from the 16th century houses a small archaeological museum. The standard tour covers most of these.

## Dinosaur Footprints and the Old Olive Tree

The archipelago has more than 200 dinosaur footprints preserved in the rock along the shoreline. The prints are about 100 million years old, and the island tour includes a stop at one of the sites. A small church is used as a dinosaur exhibition space.

The ancient olive tree is estimated at around 1,600 years old and still bears fruit. It stands on the tour route and is a quick stop, usually five minutes.

## Cycling on Veliki Brijun

Bicycles can be rented on the island, and cycling is a good alternative to the train for anyone who wants more time at each site. The terrain is flat to gently rolling, with shaded pine avenues. Allow around two to three hours for a loop covering the main sights. Rental costs extra and is not part of the park ticket, so confirm the current price at the rental point on arrival. Golf carts are also offered for an additional fee.

## Swimming and Boat Trips

Swimming on Veliki Brijun is limited to designated spots, and the standard ticket slot leaves little time for it. For a swim, a panoramic boat trip from Fažana is the better option. Shared tours start around €16–€35 and last 1.5 to 2 hours. Tours with a swim stop run longer. Glass-bottom boats and sunset dolphin-watching trips depart from Fažana. Private boats start around €240 for a day. Sveti Jerolim, a nearby island, is open to visitors only from June 1 to September 15.

## Best Time to Visit

May, June and September balance warm weather with smaller crowds. July and August are the busiest, with up to twelve boats a day and the highest €50 fare. From October, the same visit drops to €35, though some programs shorten. In summer, the €15 evening ticket from 6 pm is a cheaper way in, and it also gives access to evening events.

## Insider Tips

- Book the earliest departure of the day. The train and the Safari Park are quieter, and temperatures are lower.
- Bring water, a hat and sun cream. Shade is limited between stops.
- Buy tickets online in July and August.
- Wear walking shoes if you plan to explore the Roman villa area on foot.
- Eat before or after the trip. Food on the island is limited and priced for tourists.

## FAQ

See the FAQ section below for quick answers on tickets, timing and logistics.

faq.question: How much does it cost to visit Brijuni National Park?
faq.answer: An adult guided excursion costs €50 from June to September and €35 from October to May. The price includes the boat from Fažana, a guide, the tourist train, the Safari Park and the museum displays. Children aged 7–18 pay €20 in summer and €15 off-season.

faq.question: How do you get to Brijuni from Pula?
faq.answer: Drive or take a bus to Fažana, about 8 km north of Pula. The park boat to Veliki Brijun takes roughly 15 minutes. Tickets are sold at the Fažana marina or online.

faq.question: How long does a visit to Brijuni take?
faq.answer: The standard excursion runs in a fixed slot of about four hours. This includes the 15-minute crossing each way and about an hour on the tourist train. Cyclists should allow extra time for the island loop.

faq.question: What is the Brijuni Safari Park?
faq.answer: It is a zoo-style park that began as Tito's collection of animals, many received as gifts from foreign leaders. It holds zebras, camels, llamas, zebu cattle and an elephant. It is included in the standard park ticket.

faq.question: Can you swim in Brijuni?
faq.answer: Swimming is possible but limited on a standard visit, since the schedule is mostly sightseeing. A panoramic boat trip from Fažana with a swim stop is a better choice. Sveti Jerolim is open to visitors from June 1 to September 15.

faq.question: Are dogs allowed in Brijuni National Park?
faq.answer: Dogs are allowed with a €15 dog ticket. They are not allowed in the Safari Park, on the tourist train or in the museums.

faq.question: Is Brijuni worth visiting?
faq.answer: Yes, for the mix of Roman ruins, Tito history, wildlife and dinosaur footprints. It suits half a day. Skip it if you only want a beach day, since a boat trip from Fažana is cheaper and better for swimming.

quickAnswer: The top things to do in Brijuni are the guided tour of Veliki Brijun by tourist train, the Safari Park, the Roman villa in Verige Bay, the Tito photo exhibition, the 1,600-year-old olive tree, dinosaur footprints and cycling. Tickets cost €35–€50 for adults and include the boat from Fažana.
